The Cue at the End of the Song

歌曲结束前的那个提示 · 642 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A music school arranged a concert in an old auditorium. Its choir would sing one composition with a violin, a guitar, and a brass instrument. A young pianist named Lu had been asked to play the final chord after the chorus. The composer had marked a long pause before it. At rehearsal the singers took a breath, the drummer played early, and Lu missed her cue. The audience would hear the climax fall apart. The conductor asked the cast to find a signal everyone could recognize.

2The drummer blamed Lu's rhythm. They clapped the phrase and found their timing matched. The organ player could not see the conductor. In an empty auditorium the final note's glow seemed to last forever, and the organ's echo blurred the musical beat. A former opera singer described a visual cue she used after she had sung a long phrase. She watched a colleague's shoulders. Its clarity did not depend on the sound reaching everyone at the same moment.

3The composer wanted spontaneity. He feared a moody pause would spoil the ending. A striking gesture might give the ending the wrong kind of drama. Lu proposed a short stride. A student from a ballet class showed the violinist how to move with grace. A guitarist agreed to stand farther back. Their collaboration gave the ensemble a cohesive ending without changing the melody. A quiet turn offered a more harmonious signal than an extra beat forced into a dreamy tune.

4The next rehearsal used a dynamic beat. Several singers wanted a hip hop step to make the lively chorus more exciting. The conductor moved it earlier. A stand hid the violinist's feet, so the drummer waited for a turn at shoulder height. An orchestra could learn a subtle signal without turning the climax into a disco routine. The change helped a nervous performer keep sight of what mattered while playing with more vitality.

5A singer developed a sore throat and became unavailable. The choir divided her solo between two voices. A careful blend could keep its intimacy. One was passionate, the other steady. The director made a voice call to check where the original singer took a breath. The group kept the expressive line but adjusted the mixture of voices. A teacher proposed narration for the forthcoming Christmas gig. Lu showed that the cue already gave the audience enough time to hear the change.

6The music teacher made a short demo to help them remember. She recorded the classical phrase and the revised rhythmic step alongside a line of folk music. The players could hear where the cue came in without trying to sync with a recording at full speed. A pop singer wanted to put the rough clip on a public playlist. The conductor asked her to wait for the concert so a practice mistake would not become the version everyone learned.

7On the night, a ray of light fell across the violinist's shoulder. Lu saw him turn. A singer fought her stage fright, drew a breath, and kept the phrase intact. The drummer waited. After thirteen bars the last chord sounded superb. The audience paused, then applauded. For a moment the cast looked triumphant. What had felt like a technical breakthrough to them sounded like a simple and pleasing ending to everyone else.

8After the applause the composer asked if they should write the movement into the score. Lu drew an arrow beside the twelfth bar. A student who could compose a tune might still miss a physical cue. The drummer offered to demonstrate the swing at the next rehearsal. They kept it small enough to feel spontaneous. It could work with energetic dancing or a quiet choir. A forceful signal was unnecessary. One audience member had called the ending flawless. Lu found more delight in watching a shy player explain why the arrow was there.

歌曲结束前的那个提示

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一所音乐学校要在老礼堂办音乐会。合唱团将在小提琴、吉他和一件铜管乐器的伴奏下演唱一首作品。年轻的钢琴手露要在副歌之后弹最后一个和弦。作曲家在前面标了一个长停顿。排练时，合唱队员刚吸了一口气，鼓手就提前进了，露也错过了进来的信号。照这样下去，观众会听到高潮处脱节。指挥请大家找一个人人都认得出的信号。

2鼓手觉得是露的节奏出了问题。两人拍手打了一遍，发现彼此的时机其实一致。管风琴手看不见指挥。在空荡的礼堂里，最后一音像是久久没有散去，管风琴的回声还盖住了节拍。一位曾唱过歌剧的人说，她唱完一个长乐句后，会看同伴的肩膀。这个提示看得清楚，即使大家听到声音的时间不完全一样也能用。

3作曲家希望结尾自然，担心停顿太过做作，破坏收尾。过于醒目的手势也可能造成不合适的戏剧效果。露提议迈一小步。一个上芭蕾课的学生教小提琴手怎样把动作做得优雅。一位吉他手同意往后站些。几个人配合起来，旋律原样保留，整组人的结尾也连贯起来。与其给轻柔梦幻的曲调硬加一拍，悄悄转个身更协调。

4下一次排练用了有活力的节拍。有些合唱队员想加一个街舞动作，让欢快的副歌更热闹。指挥把动作放到了前面。谱架挡住了小提琴手的脚，鼓手就改等肩部转动。乐团用一个细微的提示就能合上高潮，无须把那里变成迪斯科表演。一个容易紧张的演奏者终于看清该盯哪里，演奏也更有劲了。

5一名歌手喉咙痛，来不了了。合唱团把她的独唱分给两人。两把声音配合得好，仍能保留亲切感。一人唱得热烈，另一人唱得平稳。负责人打了语音电话，确认原先的歌手在哪里换气。大家保留了那句富有表现力的旋律，重新安排两人的声音。老师还提议在即将举行的圣诞演出里加一段旁白。露让她听，原来的提示已给观众留够了听清变化的时间。

6音乐老师录了一个简短示范，帮大家记住做法。她把古典乐句和修改后的节奏动作录下来，旁边又录了一句民歌。演奏者不必跟着全速录音走，也能听清提示在什么时候出现。一位唱流行音乐的学生想把这个粗剪版放进公开播放列表。指挥请她等正式演出，以免大家把排练时的错误当成标准版。

7演出当晚，一道光落在小提琴手肩上。露看到他转身。一位歌手压住上台的紧张，吸一口气，把那句完整唱了下来。鼓手等着。十三小节后，最后的和弦听来极好。观众静了一瞬，然后鼓掌。台上的人一时都露出成功的喜悦。对他们来说，那是一道技术难关。在观众耳中，只是一个简单、好听的结尾。

8掌声过后，作曲家问要不要把动作写进乐谱。露在第十二小节旁画了一个箭头。学生会写旋律，也可能漏掉一个身体动作。鼓手愿意在下次排练时示范怎样转动。他们把动作做得很小，保持自然。它既能配合热烈的舞蹈，也能配合安静的合唱，用不着特别用力。有人说这个结尾无可挑剔。露更高兴的是，一位害羞的演奏者后来主动解释了那个箭头为什么在那里。
